intro: A Portland songwriter who was mostly a solo act.
story: Ashleigh Flynn, a Portland singer-songwriter raised in Kentucky and Virginia, played Pickathon in 2006 as a mostly solo artist. She later formed the all-female band Ashleigh Flynn & The Riveters with guitarist Nancy Luca. Their first album came out in late 2018, produced by Chris Funk of The Decemberists, and Good Morning, Sunshine followed on Blackbird in April 2025.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 4 pm, Fir Meadows

act: CJ Chenier & the Red Hot Louisiana Band
intro: Zydeco bandleader and son of Clifton Chenier.
story: CJ Chenier, the son of Clifton Chenier, the first Creole musician to win a Grammy, led his father's Red Hot Louisiana Band when it played Pickathon in 2006. He had taken over the band after Clifton died in 1987. In 1992 he played accordion on a Gin Blossoms track and appeared on Austin City Limits, and in 2001 he recorded Step It Up! at Dockside Studios in Maurice, Louisiana.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 6 pm, Mountain View

intro: A banjo player at home in punk, jazz and bluegrass.
story: By the time Danny Barnes played Pickathon in 2006, he had worked with Robert Earl Keen, Bill Frisell and Wayne Horvitz and was making solo records from Washington State. Pizza Box came out on Dave Matthews's ATO label in 2010 with Matthews singing backup, and NPR and Rolling Stone both took notice.
sets: Sat Aug 5, 2:30 pm, Mountain View · Sat Aug 5, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A founding voice of new acoustic fiddle.
story: Darol Anger, a fiddler who had played with the David Grisman Quintet, was already a founding voice of new acoustic music when he played Pickathon in 2006. He shared a Grammy nomination for Best Traditional Folk Album with Fiddlers 4, taught at Berklee, where he is now professor emeritus, and received the IBMA Distinguished Achievement Award in 2020. He leads the quartet Mr Sun.
sets: Sat Aug 5, 1 pm, Mountain View · Sat Aug 5, 10 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An Iowa folk singer with a gravel baritone.
story: Greg Brown, the Iowa folk singer, played Pickathon in 2006, the year The Evening Call came out. He has two Grammy nominations for Best Traditional Folk Album, one for Friend of Mine, shared with Bill Morrissey, and one for Slant 6 Mind. In 2010 he sang the part of Hades on Anais Mitchell's folk opera Hadestown.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 7:30 pm, Mountain View

intro: An Arkansas-born singer with a plainspoken voice.
story: Iris DeMent, the Arkansas-born singer who began with Infamous Angel on Philo in 1992, played Pickathon in 2006. She has two Grammy nominations for Best Contemporary Folk Album and received the Americana Music Association's Trailblazer Award in 2017, presented by John Prine. Workin' on a World, her seventh album, came out in February 2023, and Rolling Stone called it a stirring political statement.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 9 pm, Mountain View

intro: A small Pacific Northwest group.
story: Juanita Family Band, a Pacific Northwest group that formed in 2005, played Pickathon in 2006.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 4:45 pm, Mountain View · Fri Aug 4, 11:45 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A slide guitarist who began as a jazz bassist.
story: Kelly Joe Phelps, who started as a jazz bassist before turning to lap-style slide guitar, played Pickathon in 2006, twelve years after his debut, Lead Me On. His records are still studied by slide players, and Roll Away the Stone appears in The Penguin Guide to Blues Recordings. Americana UK later said he reinvented country blues for a new audience, and The Guardian ran an obituary when he died in 2022.
sets: Sat Aug 5, 10 pm, Mountain View

intro: A New England songwriter with a loyal following.
story: Kris Delmhorst, a New England songwriter, played Pickathon in 2006 with Five Stories and Songs for a Hurricane behind her. Her tenth album, Ghosts in the Garden, came out on Big Bean Music in March 2025, recorded in a farmhouse in Parsonsfield, Maine, and Americana Highways and No Depression both reviewed it.
sets: Sat Aug 5, 2 pm, Fir Meadows · Sat Aug 5, 5 pm, Fir Meadows · Sat Aug 5, 9 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A West Virginia-born Portland songwriter.
story: Little Sue, the stage name of Susannah Weaver, grew up in West Virginia and moved to Portland in 1992. She played Pickathon in 1999, 2000, 2001, 2003 and 2006. She later opened for Bob Dylan, crowdfunded a 2013 album with proceeds going to local groups, and in 2019 released Gold, her seventh album of original songs, the year the Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted her.

intro: A singer from the Reeltime Travelers.
story: Martha Scanlan sang with the Reeltime Travelers, heard on the soundtrack to the film Cold Mountain, before she played Pickathon in 2006 as a solo act. Her first solo album, The West Was Burning, was called an instant classic by Dirty Linen, and Tongue River Stories followed in 2011, written on a Montana ranch. Her song "Higher Rock" appeared on a 2025 record by Robert Plant's Saving Grace.
sets: Sat Aug 5, 7 pm, Mountain View · Sat Aug 5, 11 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A North Carolina trio that was building a following.
story: The Avett Brothers, a trio from Concord, North Carolina, played Pickathon in 2006, the year Four Thieves Gone: The Robbinsville Sessions came out on Ramseur. Judd Apatow co-directed a 2017 documentary about them, May It Last. Their 2024 self-titled album was praised by Uncut and Mojo and earned a 2025 Grammy nomination for Best Recording Package.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 7 pm, Fir Meadows · Sat Aug 5, 8:30 pm, Mountain View · Sun Aug 6, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: A San Francisco old-time banjo band.
story: The Earl Brothers, San Francisco's hard-driving old-time banjo band led by Robert Earl Davis, played Pickathon in 2005 and again in 2006.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 8:30 pm, Fir Meadows · Sat Aug 5, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: An Athens, Georgia bluegrass quintet.
story: The Packway Handle Band, an Athens, Georgia bluegrass quintet formed in 2001, played Pickathon in 2006. They were finalists in the Telluride Bluegrass Festival band competition in 2002, 2003 and 2004, taking second in 2004. Later came Take It Like a Man on Yep Roc, produced by Jim White, and a tour with Kid Rock and Foreigner that ended in September 2015.
sets: Fri Aug 4, 5:30 pm, Fir Meadows · Fri Aug 4, 10:30 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A San Francisco old-time string band.
story: The Stairwell Sisters, a San Francisco all-woman old-time string band formed in 2003, played Pickathon in 2006.

intro: A Winnipeg vocal trio on the rise.
story: The Wailin' Jennys, a Winnipeg trio, played Pickathon in 2006, the year Firecracker came out. The album drew a 2007 Juno nomination, and a North American airplay count ranked it the number two folk album of 2006. Bright Morning Stars won them a second Juno in 2012. The group is now Ruth Moody, Nicky Mehta and Heather Masse.

intro: A Kansas City honky-tonk and string band.
story: The Wilders, a Kansas City honky-tonk and string band that formed in 1999, played Pickathon in 2006 and returned in 2011.

intro: Two brothers with jazz and roots backgrounds.
story: Oliver Wood fronted the Atlanta band King Johnson and Chris Wood played bass in Medeski Martin & Wood when the two brothers began their duo, which played Pickathon in 2006. They later became a trio with Jano Rix. Kingdom in My Mind, built from jam sessions, came out in January 2020, and Heart Is the Hero followed in 2023, recorded without computer screens.

story: Trashcan Joe, a jazz act, played Pickathon in 2003 and again in 2006.

intro: A Tennessee alt-country duo.
story: The everybodyfields, an alt-country duo from Johnson City, Tennessee, played Pickathon in 2006 and again in 2008. Sam Quinn's song "T.V.A." won the 2005 Chris Austin Songwriting Contest at MerleFest, and Harp magazine described them as stompin' and twangin' in world-class style. After the 2009 split, Jill Andrews released her first full-length solo album, The Mirror, in 2011, the year of the band's reunion shows at Bristol Rhythm & Roots.
